name: # literature support is thin or contested say so explicitly in notes --
CO fundamental
notes: Strong in cool SN/AGB ejecta; band head at 4.67 um with a red-degraded P-branch. Detected in SN 1987A from ~day 160 onward (Danziger et al. 1991; Liu & Dalgarno 1995; Matsuura et al. 2024 JWST MIRI/MRS) and in SN 2004et/2017eaw with JWST (Shahbandeh et al. 2023, MNRAS 523, 6048; Kotak et al. 2005 for ground-based precedent)

name: CO first overtone
notes: Band heads at 2.294 2.323 2.353 2.383 2.414 um; the classic NIR CO signature; detected in SN 1987A (Catchpole et al. 1988) and routinely in Type II SNe CSM/ejecta

name: CO second overtone
notes: Weak; needs high column; rarely reported in SNe, included for completeness

name: SiO fundamental
notes: Broad; overlaps the amorphous silicate feature so the two must be fitted together. Detected in SN 1987A (Roche et al. 1991; Kotak et al. 2005) and tentatively in JWST spectra of several Type II SNe (Shahbandeh et al. 2023; Van Dyk et al. 2024 for SN 2023ixf); position/width here follow gas-phase band-head systematics, not a single lab measurement

name: SiO first overtone
notes: Band heads near 4.00-4.10 um; weaker than the fundamental, rarely isolated from the CO fundamental red wing

name: SiS fundamental
notes: PREDICTED to be abundant in O/C-rich ejecta zones by chemical-kinetic models (Sarangi & Cherchneff 2013, ApJ 776, 107; Cherchneff Talbi & Cernicharo 2025, A&A, arXiv:2510.01079 -- predict SiS can exceed SiO in mass by day ~400-500) but as of 2024 no unambiguous JWST spectral detection has been published for any CCSN; treat an identification here as tentative and check for corroborating SiO/CO

name: AlO B-X (0-0)
notes: Electronic band; optical not JWST but kept for cross-instrument work

name: AlO fundamental
notes: Vibrational band; blends with the 11.3 um PAH and SiC features; UNCERTAIN position, estimated from harmonic scaling of the electronic-band force constant, not a direct lab IR measurement -- treat with caution

name: CS fundamental
notes: PREDICTED minor condensation-chemistry product in S/C-rich zones (Sarangi & Cherchneff 2013); not yet robustly isolated in any published CCSN JWST spectrum, would blend with SiO fundamental red wing and PAH 7.7 complex

name: CO2 fundamental (gas)
notes: PREDICTED by ejecta chemistry models (Sarangi & Cherchneff 2013; Liljegren et al. 2020, A&A 642, A135) as a trace species; NOT YET DETECTED in a CCSN spectrum as of this writing; would overlap the CO2 ice 4.27 um feature and the CO fundamental blue wing -- gas vs ice CO2 are not separable from peak position alone, only from profile shape

name: H2O bending
notes: Gas-phase; broad and easily confused with the 6.2 um PAH and 6.2 um H2O ice bands

name: PAH 3.3
notes: Aromatic C-H stretch; the cleanest PAH band in the NIR (Tielens 2008, ARA&A 46, 289; Li & Draine 2001, ApJ 554, 778)

name: PAH 6.2
notes: Ionised-PAH tracer; peak position is a diagnostic itself -- "class A" sources peak ~6.2, "class B" (more processed/aged dust, e.g. some evolved stars and SN-like environments) peak nearer 6.3 (Peeters et al. 2002, A&A 390, 1089); if you see this shifted redward of 6.22 in a SN host region, that classification matters more than the centroid alone

name: PAH 7.7
notes: A complex of (at least) 7.6 and 7.8 um sub-features plus a 7.9 um shoulder; usually the strongest PAH band (Peeters et al. 2002; Draine & Li 2007, ApJ 657, 810 Table for the PAH emission model used in most SED codes)

name: PAH 8.6
notes: Sits on the blue wing of the silicate feature; degenerate with that continuum unless the silicate is fitted first

name: PAH 11.0
notes: Blue shoulder/sub-feature of the 11.2-11.3 complex, usually attributed to cationic PAHs (Hony et al. 2001, A&A 370, 1030); NOTE the literature convention split -- ISO/Spitzer papers usually call the main neutral-PAH peak "11.2", JWST/ground papers studying SNe often call the same physical band "11.3"; they are the same feature, not two bands, see the PAH 11.3 row below

name: PAH 11.3
notes: Neutral-PAH tracer; overlaps forsterite 11.3 and SiC 11.3 crystalline/solid-state bands -- at MIRI MRS resolution (R~1500-3500) these are only separable by profile width and shape (PAH: ~0.15-0.3 um FWHM asymmetric; SiC/forsterite: narrower, more symmetric), not by centroid alone. Also referred to as "11.2" in older ISO/Spitzer PAH literature (Hony et al. 2001)

name: PAH 12.7
notes: Blends with [Ne II] 12.81 at low/moderate resolution

name: PAH 13.5
notes: Weak; part of the Hony et al. (2001) 11-15 um decomposition

name: PAH 14.2
notes: Weak

name: PAH 16.4
notes: Van Kerckhoven et al. 2000, A&A 357, 1013

name: PAH 17.4
notes: Van Kerckhoven et al. 2000; Smith et al. 2007, ApJ 656, 770 (SINGS)

name: PAH 17.8
notes: Overlaps the red wing of the 15-20 um PAH plateau and the blue wing of the 18 um silicate feature

name: PAH plateau 6-9
notes: Broad underlying continuum/plateau beneath the 6.2/7.7/8.6 discrete features (Peeters et al. 2004; Smith et al. 2007); often attributed to a distribution of larger/more irregular PAHs or PAH clusters. Must be fitted as a separate broad component or it will bias the 7.7 feature flux

name: PAH plateau 11-15
notes: Broad plateau under the 11.3/12.0/12.7/13.5/14.2 features (Hony et al. 2001); position/strength ratio to the discrete features is itself used as a PAH processing/size diagnostic

name: PAH plateau 15-20
notes: Broad plateau under 16.4/17.4/17.8 (Van Kerckhoven et al. 2000; Smith et al. 2007); at low S/N this plateau is easy to mistake for silicate 18 um continuum curvature -- fit silicate first

name: Silicate 9.7 (generic/astronomical)
notes: Generic "astronomical silicate" (Draine & Lee 1984, ApJ 285, 89; Draine 2003, ARA&A 41, 241) -- use this row when composition is unknown. In emission or absorption depending on optical depth and geometry. Peak genuinely varies ~9.1-10.5 um with Mg/Fe content (see composition-resolved rows below) and the whole profile broadens/redshifts for CDE grain shapes vs Mie spheres of the same material (Bohren & Huffman 1983; Min et al. 2003, A&A 404, 35) and for larger grains

name: Silicate 9.7 (Mg-rich olivine)
notes: Forsterite-normative amorphous olivine glass; peak near 9.3 um, blueward of the Fe-rich case (Dorschner et al. 1995, A&A 300, 503; Jager et al. 2003, A&A 408, 193). UNCERTAIN exact centroid for a given SN -- depends on the actual Mg# of condensed grains, which is not independently known a priori

name: Silicate 9.7 (Fe-rich olivine)
notes: Fe substitution shifts and broadens the feature redward of the Mg end-member (Dorschner et al. 1995); laboratory glasses with Fe/(Mg+Fe) > 0.4 push the peak toward 10.5 um and add a weak 18-20 um red excess

name: Silicate 9.7 (amorphous pyroxene)
notes: Pyroxene-stoichiometry glass; narrower and slightly blueward of olivine glass of the same Mg/Fe (Jager et al. 1994, A&A 292, 641; Dorschner et al. 1995) -- olivine vs pyroxene network connectivity, not just Mg/Fe, sets the exact shape

name: Silicate 18 (generic/astronomical)
notes: Partner of the 9.7 um feature; their flux ratio constrains grain size and optical depth (Draine & Lee 1984). Widened the red edge relative to the original entry (to 24 um) because lab olivine/pyroxene bending-mode complexes genuinely extend that far (Jager et al. 2003; Demyk et al. 2017, A&A 606, A50)

name: Silicate 18 (olivine bend)
notes: Olivine-glass bending complex tends to peak bluer (~16-19 um) than pyroxene glass of similar Mg/Fe (Jager et al. 2003; Demyk et al. 2017, 2022 A&A 666, A192 low-T constants)

name: Silicate 18 (pyroxene bend)
notes: Pyroxene-glass bending complex tends to peak redder (~20-21 um) than olivine glass (Jager et al. 2003; Demyk et al. 2017); UNCERTAIN -- lab-to-lab scatter in this sub-feature is larger than for the 9.7 um stretch

name: Forsterite 11.3
notes: Narrow; overlaps PAH 11.3/11.2 and SiC 11.3 -- the three are separable only at MRS resolution by linewidth (Koike et al. 2003, A&A 399, 1101; Molster & Waters 2003)

name: Forsterite 27.6
notes: Near the MRS ch4-long red cutoff where calibration is poorest. (A further forsterite band near 33.6/69 um is a well-known temperature diagnostic -- Koike et al. 2006, A&A 449, 583 -- but both lie beyond your stated 28 um working range, so only noted here, not tabulated.)

name: Forsterite 33.6
notes: Beyond MRS coverage

name: Enstatite 24.5
notes: Individual resonances per Koike et al. 2000 (Icarus 145, 541) and Chihara et al. 2002 (A&A 391, 267) lab spectra; crystalline silicates are not yet robustly identified in any JWST CCSN spectrum as of 2024 -- flagged here as "what to look for", not "what has been seen"

name: SiC 11.3
notes: Carbon-star dust signature (Treffers & Cohen 1974, ApJ 188, 545) genuinely degenerate with PAH 11.3/11.2 and forsterite 11.3 at low/moderate resolution. Profile is the only discriminant: SiC alpha-polytype peaks ~11.3 um and is fairly symmetric; beta-SiC/smaller or more irregular grains shift and broaden it toward 10.6-11.0 um (Speck et al. 2005, ApJ 634, 426; Pegourie 1988, A&A 194, 335). No credible SiC detection in any CCSN JWST spectrum has been published as of this writing -- SiC is an AGB/carbon-star signature by analogy, carried here as a candidate degeneracy, not a confirmed CCSN species

name: Amorphous carbon
notes: No band structure; shows up only as continuum slope -- listed so it is not forgotten as a dust candidate. Optical constants: Zubko et al. 1996, MNRAS 282, 1321; Rouleau & Martin 1991, ApJ 377, 526; Hanner 1988 "AC" grains used in many SN dust-mass fits (e.g. Wesson et al. 2015, MNRAS 446, 2089; Bevan 2018, MNRAS 480, 4659)

name: Graphite (featureless, MIR)
notes: CORRECTED from the previous "Graphite 11.5" entry: I could not find a credible laboratory or astronomical basis for a localised graphite band at 11.5 um in this wavelength range. Graphite's only strong, well-established spectral signature is the 2175 Angstrom UV bump (Stecher 1965), far outside JWST coverage; in the mid-IR, graphite (like amorphous carbon) is essentially featureless (Draine & Lee 1984; Draine 2003). Recommend DROPPING the old 11.5 um row unless you have a specific source for it -- I have replaced it with this featureless-continuum entry so the species is not silently lost from the table

name: HAC continuum
notes: Rising/curved featureless continuum carrying weak superimposed C-H bands (see the aliphatic rows below); optical constants and model: Jones et al. 2013 (A&A 558, A62, THEMIS); Duley & Williams 1981 (MNRAS 196, 269); Grishko & Duley 2002 (ApJ 568, 448). A plausible CCSN carbon-dust carrier alongside amorphous carbon, not yet uniquely distinguished from it in any SN spectrum published to date

name: Aliphatic C-H stretch 3.4
notes: NEW KIND. Satellite/complex redward of the aromatic 3.3 um PAH band, multi-component near 3.42/3.48/3.56 um (Pendleton & Allamandola 2002, ApJS 138, 75; Dartois et al. 2007, A&A 463, 635; diffuse-ISM analogue). A 3.4/3.3 flux ratio well above the typical ISM/PAH value (~2-10x weaker than 3.3 normally) is one of the better host-vs-ejecta discriminants discussed in the prose below

name: Aliphatic C-H deformation 6.85
notes: NEW KIND. Pendleton & Allamandola 2002; blends with the blue wing of the 7.7 um PAH complex and can be confused with a weak carbonate/sulfate dip in absorption-dominated spectra

name: Aliphatic C-H deformation 7.25
notes: NEW KIND. Weaker partner of the 6.85 um band (Pendleton & Allamandola 2002; Chiar et al. 2013, ApJ 770, 78)

name: Alumina amorphous 12
notes: NEW KIND. Broad single band from amorphous Al2O3 (corundum-type network); distinct from crystalline corundum (see next row). Begemann et al. 1997, ApJ 476, 199; Posch et al. 1999, A&A 352, 609 (detected in some O-rich AGB/RSG spectra). PREDICTED SN condensate (alumina is expected to be among the first high-temperature condensates -- Sarangi & Cherchneff 2015, ApJ 807, 168; Sluder et al. 2018, MNRAS 480, 5580) but not yet confirmed in any CCSN JWST spectrum

name: Corundum crystalline 16.8
notes: NEW KIND. UNCERTAIN/rare; crystalline corundum shows sharper structure near 16.8 and 21 um (Koike et al. 1995, Icarus 114, 203; Posch et al. 1999) in contrast to the broad amorphous-alumina band above

name: Corundum crystalline 21
notes: NEW KIND. See Corundum crystalline 16.8 row; UNCERTAIN, no SN detection claimed to date

name: MgO periclase 19.5
notes: NEW KIND. Single rock-salt-lattice absorption; narrower than the silicate complex it sits inside. Lab constants: Henning & Mutschke 1997, A&A 327, 743. Tentatively invoked for some O-rich AGB/RSG spectra (Speck et al. 2000, A&AS 146, 437) but CONTESTED/rare even there, and has NOT been claimed in any published CCSN spectrum -- treat strictly as a candidate

name: Silica (amorphous SiO2) 9.1
notes: NEW KIND. Amorphous silica shows a doublet-like structure near 9.1 and 21.3 um, distinguishable in principle from (Mg,Fe) silicates because it has no network-modifying cation (Fabian et al. 2000, A&A 364, 282). PREDICTED as a possible early high-temperature SN condensate (silica/silicate precursor chemistry, Sarangi & Cherchneff 2015) but essentially unconfirmed observationally in any CCSN to date; easily confused with the blue wing of the 9.7 um silicate complex

name: Silica (amorphous SiO2) 21.3
notes: NEW KIND. See Silica 9.1 row; Fabian et al. 2000; UNCERTAIN, candidate only

name: MgS 30
notes: CONTESTED carrier of the classic carbon-star "30 um feature" (first proposed by Goebel & Moseley 1985, ApJ 290, L35; Hony et al. 2002, A&A 390, 533). Mostly beyond MRS range (red edge ~28 um) for most redshifts, so this is largely a "look at the red edge of your last channel" entry. The MgS identification has a known mass-budget problem -- Zhukovska & Gail 2008 (A&A 486, 487) and Zhang, Jiang & Li 2009 (ApJ 702, 680) show the implied MgS mass can exceed the total available interstellar sulfur in some sources -- and Messenger, Speck & Volk 2013 (ApJ 764, 142) find the profile does not uniformly fit across carbon stars. In a CCSN this is an analogy import from AGB/PPNe dust chemistry, not yet detected in any CCSN JWST spectrum; report any 25-30 um excess as "consistent with a sulfide or very cold silicate/carbon continuum", not as a firm MgS identification

name: FeS 23
notes: UNCERTAIN/weakly supported even in its original AGB context -- the 23 um troilite-like band used in some dust-opacity compilations (Pollack et al. 1994, ApJ 421, 615) rests more on assumed cosmochemical sulfide abundances than on a strong, uncontested direct spectral identification; lab constants from Begemann et al. 1994 (ApJ 423, L71) / Henning & Stognienko 1996 (A&A 311, 291). PREDICTED SN condensate by chemical-kinetics models (CaS/FeS/MgS family -- Sarangi & Cherchneff 2015) but not yet confirmed in a CCSN spectrum

name: FeO 20
notes: Moved from kind=other to kind=oxide in this revision. UNCERTAIN; based on extrapolation from wuestite/iron-oxide lab optical constants (Henning & Mutschke 1997) rather than a firm astronomical identification; essentially a placeholder for "something in the Fe-O family could sit here", not a confirmed band

name: Nanodiamond C-H sp3 3.43/3.53
notes: NEW KIND. SPECULATIVE for CCSN dust. The only direct astronomical IR detection of this feature is in two Herbig Ae/Be protoplanetary disks (Guillois, Ledoux & Nenner 1999, ApJ 521, L133) -- not in any supernova. The case for an SN *origin* of presolar nanodiamonds rests on meteoritic isotopic anomalies (Lewis et al. 1987, Nature 326, 160; Clayton, Meyer & Zinner 1995/1999) and is indirect, cosmochemical evidence, not an IR spectroscopic SN detection. Include this row only to flag what to look for; do not report a detection here without extraordinary care, since the band overlaps the aliphatic 3.4 um hydrocarbon complex and is easily confused with it

name: H2O ice 3.05
notes: Deep absorption; a broad red wing indicates grain growth (Boogert, Gerakines & Whittet 2015, ARA&A 53, 541, for the general ice-band review used here and below)

name: H2O ice 6.0
notes: Overlaps the 6.2 um PAH band

name: H2O ice 13
notes: Very broad; easily absorbed into a bad continuum fit

name: CO2 ice 4.27
notes: Narrow and deep; a sensitive ice thermal-history probe

name: CO2 ice 15.2
notes: Double-peaked when crystalline (Gerakines et al. 1995, A&A 296, 810)

name: CO ice 4.67
notes: Overlaps the gas-phase CO fundamental band head

name: CH4 ice 7.7
notes: Overlaps the 7.7 um PAH complex

name: CH3OH ice 9.7
notes: In the silicate trough
